title: The sandbox tool tells the agent which shell runs its commands
user_story: As the owner I want an agent to write commands the host can run: in the live run (2026-10-28) Codex wrote POSIX `VAR=1 python ...` and Windows cmd.exe failed (agent/PLAN_6.6.4_L3.md A5).

requirements.description: sandbox_run_code's description, in the registry and on /mcp, names the shell of the configured mode: cmd.exe with its syntax for local Windows, POSIX sh for local Linux/macOS and Docker, both plus a recommendation to send Python code for auto.
The note is computed per listing; the shared tool list and the other tools' descriptions do not change, and the auto mode is not resolved (no dependency planning).

nonfunctional: Under 20 ms per listing (one settings read)
outputs: sandbox_run_code description with the shell note
postconditions: Every agent client reads the shell that will run its command before calling the tool

scenarios.expected: cmd.exe and `set VAR=1 && python` in both the registry and /mcp descriptions
Local Linux/macOS and Docker never mention cmd.exe
Auto names both shells and recommends Python code
An unknown stored mode falls back to the local shell description; registry and /mcp agree
The shared TOOLS list is not modified and other tools keep their descriptions

recovery: Fix the note at sandbox.shell_note; never resolve the auto mode while listing tools. TASK-TOOL-SHELL-664, max three cycles.
test_environment: Disposable config (tests/_env.py); platform and mode patched; evidence in docs/qa/evidence/tool-shell-664/.

tdd.scope: RED: 6 tests on 0e52f6e, 5 failing (the shared-list check passes on both). GREEN: 6/6.
